title: Permissive-Washing in the Open AI Supply Chain: A Large-Scale Audit of License Integrity

problem.claim: Permissive licenses for AI artifacts require license text, copyright notices, and upstream attribution to support lawful use, modification, and redistribution.

gap.claim: Compliance with these licensing requirements remains unverified at scale across AI supply chains.

contributions.claim: The paper audits permissive-license integrity across 294,012 dataset-model-application supply chains spanning 3,198 datasets, 6,218 models, and 26,302 applications on Hugging Face and GitHub.
The paper defines permissive washing as labeling AI artifacts as free to use while omitting the legal documentation required to make that label actionable.
The paper releases its full audit dataset and reproducible pipeline.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that 96.9% of datasets and 96.4% of models lack the required license text, while 2.1% of datasets and 2.6% of models satisfy both license-text and copyright requirements.

The authors report limited downstream attribution propagation: 25.0% of models preserve compliant dataset notices, 5.4% of applications preserve compliant model notices, and 5.9% preserve any linked upstream notice.

narrative_sequence.summary: Permissive licenses dominate open-source AI and signal broad reuse rights.
Required license documentation and attribution are not verified reliably at scale, creating legal exposure when conditions are unmet.
The paper names this mismatch between permissive labeling and required documentation permissive washing.
The authors conduct a large-scale audit of dataset-model-application supply chains across Hugging Face and GitHub.
The audit reports widespread missing license evidence and weak downstream propagation of attribution notices, followed by a recommendation to treat license files and notices as legal truth.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the audit methodology or inclusion criteria in detail.
The abstract does not report artifact-level validation procedures or error analysis.
The abstract does not specify the released dataset and pipeline contents or access conditions.
